question.text: A Cat III AIF's listed mid-cap long position (5% of NAV) is suspended by the exchange following a forensic-audit announcement; resumption is uncertain for 90+ days. The CIO receives new subscription requests next week. What is the MOST APPROPRIATE action for the Investment Manager?

answer.text: Continue marking the suspended stock at last traded price and accept new subscriptions at current NAV
Segregate the suspended position into a side-pocket (separate class) so new subscriptions and redemptions interact only with the main NAV, protecting all parties
Write the position off to zero immediately
Pause ALL fund operations until resumption

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Illiquid/suspended positions must NOT be marked at last trade under Cat III valuation rules. Side-pocket segregation is the industry-standard mechanism: (a) existing investors retain their share of the side-pocket upside/downside, (b) new subscribers only buy into the main NAV, avoiding free-riding, and (c) the illiquid mark does not whip around daily NAV. Writing off and pausing all operations are disproportionate. **The Trap:** Option A creates arbitrage for new subscribers. Option C is premature (recovery possible). Option D breaches the fund's operational commitments. **Cross-Exam Context:** Side-pocket is a Cat III-specific tool. Cross-ref: Mutual-fund side-pockets (SEBI MF Regs 2019 amendment) are conceptually similar but regulated separately. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Draft a side-pocket SOP in the PPM BEFORE any crisis: trigger criteria (suspension > X days, credit event, 30% MTM drop), admin process, communication timeline, and voluntary-consent mechanism from investors. Reactive side-pocketing during a crisis invites SEBI scrutiny.
